read: Ownership Map job_catalog (P2, ASM-A6-tables-9); Architecture v5 slide 44; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-01 and DP-05
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check

text: SCR-44 Interface and job monitor is the gateway-bff composite route over P1's job read, rerun and freshness read (DP-19, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON). The APP story serves the reads, the CON story publishes them, and the OPS story registers the route, its alerts and its runbook; no P1 story renders the screen.

text: Legacy AC3 (a late ACE batch) is owned by RWB-ITG-AD018-ITG. The P1 slice records the dependent job WAITING and the data product STALE with MSG-P1-001, and the cross-service proof runs in the ITG slice.

text: The 14 tables and 12 columns are added to the ACE schema by the ACE team's own migration, whose version is allocated on the ACE schema sequence at build time; V027__rwb_ace_001_recovery_source_additions.sql stays the legacy file name and the source of the object list. The 14 ingestion jobs stay ACE Spring Batch jobs, one per source, each writing one ace_batch_run row per source and business date.
why: The legacy story fixes V027 and the job set on the monolith schema sequence, and the target adds one schema and one login per service without restating the ACE sequence.
read: Legacy RWB-ACE-001 sections 4, 7 and 12; TSD P1 v3 T3.2
confirm: ACE team lead before the estimate
impact: Low: the object list and the field appendix are unchanged.

text: SELECT on the 14 new tables and on the 12 new columns is granted to ace_view_owner only; the 19 service logins keep SELECT on the Section B views and hold no grant on public. The row-level read of ACE data stays behind the views.
why: DP-02 gives one login per service and TSD P1 v3 T6.3 names ace_view_owner as the owner of the views and the holder of SELECT on the ACE tables.
read: TSD P1 v3 T6.3; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-02 and DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 29
confirm: ACE DBA and platform DB owner
impact: None: the boundary rule already fixes it.

text: The 14 ingestion jobs keep the ACE team's own schedule and file or API contract per source. No schedule time, cadence or interface number is written in this story; each job's number and frequency come from Interface Specifications v3 and the field appendix.
why: No source gives the target schedule of the 14 jobs, and a cadence written in a story would be a value a business person may change.
read: Legacy RWB-ACE-001 appendix A frequency column; TSD P1 v3 T5.1
impact: Low: the schedule is ACE's own and is named by reference.

text: The reconciliation read (API-P1-003, GET /admin/reconciliation/results) answers from reconciliation_result by field ID (DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129) and adds the REC-05 orphan rows with their table, column and key. No field, no count and no threshold is invented.
why: The console and the ITG harness need a fixed answer shape, and no source gives the response fields of API-P1-003.
read: TSD P1 v3 T-A.1 and T-A.2 API-P1-003; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 reconciliation_result
confirm: Recovery tech lead at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Low: the fields are the table's own.

text: JOB-04 runs as an event-started Temporal workflow on the workflow kit (DP-10, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), started by AceDataReady. P1 runs no Temporal Schedule of its own for the console; the freshness Schedule behind the stale set is rwb-case's DataQualityFreshnessCheck.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 records JOB-04 as an event-triggered workflow, and the console's Schedule is in rwb-case; DP-10 is listed on the P1 slice and must be applied somewhere.
read: Architecture v5 slide 44; RWB-P3-AD019-APP section 12.6; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-10
impact: None: the mechanism matches the job map.

text: Legacy AC3 is proved at the freshness answer and the STALE marking in rwb-source-data; the console that renders it is rwb-case's and is mocked in this story with the rwb-case contract mock. The legacy AC1 and AC2 screen behaviour stays with RWB-P3-AD019-APP and RWB-ITG-AD019-ITG.
why: The split plan gives AC3 to the P1 slice and AC1 and AC2 to the P3 and ITG slices, and the P1 slice builds no screen.
read: split_plan.json RWB-P1-AD019-APP acs [AC3]; RWB-P3-AD019-APP sections 1 and 7
impact: None: the split is recorded in the plan.

text: P1 produces the cutover extract of the legacy Workbench case, case account, case party and assignment records with their ACE business keys, and rwb-case loads the rows into rwb_case through its own cutover migration on its own Flyway sequence. P1 writes no other service's schema and no row of rwb_case.
why: The Ownership Map puts the four tables with P3, and DP-01 forbids a service writing another service's schema; the legacy key and its AC1 and AC3 are nonetheless on the P1 slice.
read: Ownership Map recovery_case, case_account, case_party, assignment (P3); RWB-ITG-DM003-ITG section 1; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-01
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check

text: The legacy extract is read once by the cutover run from the legacy Workbench cutover dump and is not landed in rwb_source_data; the ten clean days are counted from the reconciliation_result rows JOB-04 writes, and the sign-off is held in the cutover record of the release pipeline.
why: No source gives the extract format or a sign-off table, and no table may be invented for either.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-003 AC1 and AC3; Architecture v5 slide 32; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 reconciliation_result
impact: Medium: the cutover evidence is the reconciliation result and the pipeline record.

text: The ten clean days are ten consecutive business dates on which the reconciliation results of the migrated records are PASS with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan; a break resets the count. No counter table is created.
why: The legacy AC3 requires ten clean days and no source gives the counting rule or a table for it.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-003 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11; RWB-ITG-DM003-ITG section 4
impact: Low: the count is read from the results already written.

why: The Ownership Map puts the live treatment records with S2 and the DP04 copies with P1, and the ruling on dp_treatment says the copies are built from events.
